'''''Phyllostachys nigra''''', [[common name|commonly known as]] '''black bamboo'''<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate=27 February 2015}}</ref> or '''purple bamboo''' ({{lang-zh|紫竹}}), is a [[species]] of [[bamboo]], [[native plant|native]] to [[Hunan|Hunan Province]] of [[China]], and is widely cultivated elsewhere.<ref>{{cite book |chapter-url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200025925 |title=Flora of China Online |author=Zheng-ping Wang and Chris Stapleton |volume=22 |chapter=''Phyllostachys nigra'' (Loddiges ex Lindley) Munro}}</ref>

Growing up to 10 meters (35 ft) tall by 5cm (2 in) wide, it forms clumps of slender arching canes which turn black after two or three seasons. The abundant lance-shaped leaves are {{convert|4|-|13|cm|0|abbr=on}} long.

Numerous [[form (botany)|forms]] and [[cultivars]] are available for garden use. The species <ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Phyllostachys nigra'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/12869/Phyllostachys-nigra/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref> and the form ''P. nigra'' f. ''henonis''<ref name=RHS>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Phyllostachys nigra'' f. ''henonis'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/78374/Phyllostachys-nigra-f-henonis/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}}</ref> have both gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 78 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 April 2018}}</ref> The form ''henonis'' is also known as Henon bamboo<ref name=RHS/> and as [[cultivar]] 'Henon'.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bamboo.org/BambooSourceList/index.php |title=Bamboo Species Source List |publisher=American Bamboo Society |access-date=31 May 2014}}</ref>

== Life cycle ==
Like many species of bamboo, black bamboo [[Synchronous flowering|synchronizes its flowering]], with flowering events happening every 40-120 years. According to one source, it has bloomed every 120 years "since records have been kept".<ref>{{cite book | editor-last1= Burley|editor-first1= J. |editor-last2=Styles |editor-first2= B.T. |first= Daniel| last= Janzen | date= 1976 | title= Tropical Trees | location= London| publisher= Academic Press | pages= 138-139}}</ref> It is [[monocarpic]], that is, after flowering, the plants die.

Henon bamboo flowers every 120 years and is predicted to flower in the 2020s. Since it is widely distributed in Japan, dieback of its stands may cause serious social and environmental problems. Moreover, Henon bamboo rarely sets fertile seeds, so it is not clear how this species has survived over long periods in Japan.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yamada |first1=Toshihiro |last2=Imada |first2=Karin |last3=Aoyagi |first3=Hitoshi |last4=Nakabayashi |first4=Miyabi |date=2023-06-12 |title=Does monocarpic Phyllostachys nigra var. henonis regenerate after flowering in Japan? Insights from 3 years of observation after flowering |journal=PLOS ONE |language=en |volume=18 |issue=6 |article-number=e0287114 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0287114 |issn=1932-6203 |pmc=10259779 |pmid=37307263 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Flowering for naught: 120 years with nothing to show |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2023/09/230901124058.htm |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=ScienceDaily |language=en}}</ref>

== Uses ==
It is used for [[lumber]] (timber), food, and musical instruments, among other things, in areas of China where it is native and also worldwide.

==Phytochemistry==

A 2008 study from [[Zhejiang University]], in [[China]], isolated several [[Flavones|flavone]] [[C-glycoside|C-glycosides]] on black bamboo leaves, including [[orientin]], [[homoorientin]], [[vitexin]] and [[isovitexin]].<ref>Isolation and purification of four flavone C-glycosides from antioxidant of bamboo leaves by macroporous resin column chromatography and preparative high-performance liquid chromatography. Yu Zhang, Jingjing Jiao, Chengmei Liu, Xiaoqin Wu and Ying Zhang, ''[[Food Chemistry (journal)|Food Chemistry]]'', 1 April 2008,, Volume 107, Issue 3, Pages 1326–1336, {{doi|10.1016/j.foodchem.2007.09.037}}</ref>
